assumptions.rationale: Educated assumption: Kim’s March reelection occurred within the party-controlled assembly; competitive electoral accountability is absent.
Educated assumption: Assembly election within party rule is the implemented selection route, rather than delegation to a panel selected for expertise.
Educated assumption: Article 65 rejects education-based exclusion but excludes people described as having mental disabilities. The franchise is broad, yet not universal.

Educated assumption: For the cabinet premier, articles 93 and 119–124 subordinate administrative action to assembly legislation. Kim’s separate head-of-state powers are not transferred to the premier.
Educated assumption: Opposition has no realistic route to compete or take office; formal party-activity guarantees do not provide equal electoral conditions.
Educated assumption: Budget scrutiny occurs within controlled institutions; the absence of independent opposition prevents opposition-led investigation of public spending.
Educated assumption: Party interference in adjudication prevents an independent constitutional check on executive decisions.
Educated assumption: The assembly selects national leadership; affiliated unions mobilize people rather than exercise a separate power to choose the government.
Educated assumption: The enforced party monopoly excludes political competition, supporting leadership control over which political organizations may contest elections.
Educated assumption: Law-making is assigned to controlled state organs, with no voter repeal mechanism in the reviewed constitutional framework.
Educated assumption: The 2026 changes institutionalize leader-directed state affairs; commission and cabinet functions operate beneath that overarching authority.

Educated assumption: The assembly can formally recall the cabinet premier, but noncompetitive elections and paramount leadership control prevent an independent representative check for serious abuse. Moderate disagreement retains that statutory power and distinguishes the premier from the supreme leader; it does not claim every internal dismissal is impossible. This interprets implemented institutions, not an official questionnaire response; the exact normative preference is inferred.

Educated assumption: Leadership control and the constitutional exceptional extension provision favour postponement without genuinely independent approval. The exact continuity-only condition is not verified; moderate agreement is more likely than unrestricted legal permission.

Educated assumption: Formal accountability to electors and official removal coexist with tightly controlled elections. A freely initiated, defined popular recall vote was not verified; moderate disagreement is the likelier practical interpretation, rather than denying every formal recall provision.
Educated assumption: Leader supremacy and removal of the assembly’s recall power leave the supreme executive without effective electoral or legislative accountability.
Educated assumption: The armed forces are constitutionally subordinate to the supreme commander, supporting rejection of an independent military power to replace him.
Educated assumption: Drug use is criminalized in the documented legal baseline; later research describes expanded punishment. This opposes a general personal-risk exemption.

Educated assumption: Identity-linked communication controls and surveillance support investigatory monitoring, including the narrower court-authorized case; independent judicial safeguards are not claimed.
Educated assumption: Independent assembly is suppressed; peaceful demonstrators have no practical entitlement to obstruct roads under the proposed safeguards.

Educated assumption: Enforced health and movement measures indicate acceptance of paternal health direction. Self-protection alone is not separately established from infection control, so agreement is qualified.

Educated assumption: Sustained monitoring and residence controls make long retention of ordinary movement information likely. The exact retention period is unavailable; this is not a verified multi-year statutory rule.

Educated assumption: Routine movement checks and coercive policing suggest acceptance of preventive driver checks. Intoxication testing without suspicion was not specifically documented, making moderate agreement a tentative extension.

Educated assumption: Preventive restrictions are implemented, although genuine independent court safeguards are absent. The statement would permit a narrower, court-supported intervention; moderate agreement is likely without claiming such hearings operate.
Educated assumption: Obtained smartphone software links users, SIMs and devices to state-managed identifiers used for service access; device registration is also required.

Educated assumption: Reported inspections and searches operate without individual suspicion even outside a credible violence alert. Acceptance of this narrower security-search permission is the likelier interpretation.
Educated assumption: The suppression of independent gatherings supports authority to prohibit gatherings under the narrower serious-disorder condition.
Educated assumption: Independent reporting contrary to official positions is punishable; exposing misconduct does not provide the proposed publication freedom.

Educated assumption: The reproduced 2009 law forbids ordinary citizen ownership while allowing separately authorised use. Strong disagreement with private self-defence ownership is likelier; the source is a historical reproduced statute, not an independently verified consolidated 2026 text.

Educated assumption: Political-security detention lacks effective independent judicial scrutiny. Strong agreement is likely for indefinite threat-based detention, qualified because a distinct terrorism-specific termination rule was not verified.

Educated assumption: Foreign arrivals must comply with content restrictions in consular guidance; Article 39 prioritises national culture against disallowed external influence. Infer priority in a conflict, qualified by actual accommodation of the Chinese community.

Educated assumption: A common national framework dominates public institutions, despite verified accommodation for Chinese community schooling. Moderate disagreement is more likely than either categorical exclusion or a general spending entitlement.

Educated assumption: Article 53 promotes the socialist way of life and Article 54 applies national linguistic character across society. Infer an expectation that settlers adopt common norms, while Chinese schools show that adoption need not erase every inherited custom.

Educated assumption: Chinese pupils retain a community institution while being encouraged to contribute to DPRK society. At the same time, authorities police disallowed Southern influence. This supports selective cultural retention rather than either unconditional acceptance or compulsory abandonment of every foreign identity.

Educated assumption: Article 54 gives the Pyongyang language an explicit public priority, with recent speech policing illustrating implementation. Infer national-language priority, qualified by the functioning Chinese school; no claim that every foreign-language service is banned.

Educated assumption: National ceremonial identity is framed around the common Korean nation and revolutionary history. A separate Indigenous ceremonial category was not identified; moderate disagreement is a provisional extension, not a claim that ethnic minorities do not exist.

Educated assumption: Articles 39 and 50 direct state cultural work toward national heritage and national artistic forms. The completed celadon project illustrates institutional implementation. Infer the spending priority from that mandate, without claiming a measured budget share or treating UNESCO funding as domestic expenditure.

Educated assumption: The reported naming directive subordinates family cultural choices to state-defined national identity; contemporary language policing reinforces that priority. Distinct identities therefore do not prevail when authorities judge them incompatible. Permitted Chinese festivities do not reverse that conflict rule.

Educated assumption: The common national revolutionary calendar governs public life. Chinese festival recognition qualifies the interpretation but does not establish routinely rescheduled national services.

Educated assumption: Articles 39 and 53 define the national cultural project through socialist national continuity and reject conflicting ways of life. Infer qualified disagreement with incorporating several distinct cultural traditions into national identity; Chinese community recognition prevents treating this as complete exclusion of foreign traditions.

Educated assumption: Integration into nationally prescribed language and collective life is the likely programme emphasis. Permission for distinct Chinese schooling is counterevidence to total cultural uniformity; migrant programme details remain limited.

Educated assumption: Protected national language and restricted foreign cultural influence favour national-language signage. Moderate disagreement is an estimate; neither tourist translations nor enclave signage was comprehensively surveyed.

Educated assumption: RFA’s March 2025 resident interviews report directives requiring names that express revolutionary loyalty and national identity, including a specific ordered change of a name construed as disloyal. Infer strong preference for family transmission of shared state-defined identity over competing community choices; these are reported directives, not verified universal compliance.

Educated assumption: Religious expression remains subordinate to general state-order controls. A special burqa exemption from comparable face-covering prohibitions is unlikely, but no exact provision was verified.

Educated assumption: The state prescribes a shared socialist cultural life, but supports an identifiable Chinese community school and officials join its festivities. Infer a predominant common national identity with limited community accommodation, rather than equal incorporation of distinct ways of life.

Educated assumption: National linguistic and socialist-cultural requirements favour common customs. Moderate agreement remains qualified by implemented Chinese community exceptions rather than assuming all distinct customs are banned.

Educated assumption: Highly controlled entry and residence make restrictive intake likely. A published housing-and-workforce annual numerical cap was not found, so only moderate agreement with that specific formulation is warranted.

Educated assumption: Residence is conditional on national permission and controlled purposes, making a general settlement entitlement for better living conditions unlikely. Permits alone do not prove categorical refusal; disagreement is qualified.

Educated assumption: Entry law permits several purposes, including political protection and family-related residence, not solely needed skills. Moderate disagreement is likely; ordinary permanent-route practice remains opaque.
Educated assumption: Family residence provisions make qualified reunion more likely than categorical exclusion. Eligibility and enforcement for every permanently settled migrant are not verified.

Educated assumption: Article 79 specifies politically defined grounds of asylum, rather than an unrestricted right to permanent settlement for anyone fleeing a home country. Infer qualified disagreement with the broad entitlement; the text does provide protection and does not establish a skills requirement.

Educated assumption: Article 56 allows expulsion for serious immigration violations; KCNA’s September 2023 announcement applied expulsion to King’s unauthorised entry. Infer opposition to a general right to remain, without treating every irregular entrant as automatically deported.

Educated assumption: State permission remains controlling despite potential economic gains from foreign labour. Moderate agreement is the likelier estimate, rather than proof of a published employer-demand cap.

Educated assumption: Resource-constrained central allocation makes additional service burdens a likely reason to limit arrivals. This is a tentative estimate of the specified rationale, not a verified housing-driven reduction policy.

Educated assumption: Central permission is likely to treat family entry as part of managed admission rather than an unlimited exemption. No exact common annual numerical cap was documented, limiting confidence.

Educated assumption: A job offer does not remove national entry and residence authorisation. Moderate disagreement is more likely than treating an offer as a general admission entitlement; actual work-route criteria remain incompletely documented.

Educated assumption: Verified residence depends on permitted purpose and institutional arrangements. Sponsorship is a likely ordinary control, although an exclusive employer-or-family requirement was not established.
Educated assumption: National residence permission is distinct from university attendance. Graduation alone is unlikely to confer a settlement route; no precise graduate transition rule was found.

Educated assumption: The entry law allows protection for politically persecuted foreigners. That makes qualified entry beyond ordinary economic intake likely; the exact numerical-limit exemption remains unverified.

Educated assumption: National compatriot recognition and long-standing Chinese community arrangements favour some cultural familiarity. Moderate agreement is an estimate, since diplomacy and political alignment also shape access.

Educated assumption: National social allocation and restricted residence make broad noncitizen cash-benefit or housing access unlikely. Constitutional protection of foreigners qualifies this estimate; exact benefit eligibility was not verified.
Educated assumption: Foreign cultural accommodation does not establish a numerical expansion because cultures differ. National cultural integration makes qualified disagreement the likelier response.

Educated assumption: Section 6 permits nuclear use before specified attacks materialise; the September 2026 warning invokes that policy. This supports force before the country has been attacked, restricted to claimed security contingencies rather than arbitrary expansion.

Educated assumption: The September analysis records high preconditions for US talks alongside military signaling. The government maintains nuclear force as its security foundation. Infer qualified disagreement with giving slower diplomacy priority; this does not deny its extensive diplomacy with partners.

Educated assumption: The approved 2026 budget allocates 15.8% to defence, including expanded deterrence and combat capability. Infer willingness to carry substantial costs to gain military advantage; the figure does not prove superiority has been attained.

Educated assumption: Article 85 requires service according to law. March 2026 reporting describes actual spring conscription, including male eligibility standards and a high proportion of school graduates listed. Together these support compulsory male service for force readiness; the small reported sample is not a national rate.

Educated assumption: In March 2026 Kim rejected nuclear disarmament in return for economic benefits or security guarantees. September’s foreign-minister statement reinforces the sovereignty red line. Infer reluctance to weaken strategic standing through substantial concessions, while leaving room for less consequential diplomacy.

Educated assumption: Military AI investment and unmanned development favour operational autonomy when useful. Moderate agreement is a provisional per-attack-approval estimate; neither autonomous lethal deployment nor an adopted permission rule was verified.

Educated assumption: The nuclear law identifies deterrence and repelling aggression as its main mission, but the government has also committed troops to sustained combat abroad in Russia. This is a supported combination of defensive purpose and expeditionary practice, rather than a claim that either is absent.

Educated assumption: Troops initially dispatched in October 2024 were publicly acknowledged in combat in April 2025, with losses and continued support recognised. This sustained deployment supports maintaining a force able to fight beyond national borders; no unverified troop totals or worldwide reach are claimed.

Educated assumption: Coercive military signaling weighs against a categorical preference to leave disputes unresolved. Moderate disagreement is likelier, while the new territorial definition and absence of an explicit war-to-settle-boundaries policy prevent a stronger claim.

Educated assumption: The September 16 defence-ministry statement warns the US that its WMD-response cooperation could prompt invocation of the nuclear law. Infer use of threatened force to change an opponent’s conduct in a serious dispute, without claiming that concessions actually resulted.

Educated assumption: The government combines renewed nuclear warnings with weapons signaling and demanding diplomatic preconditions. Infer willingness to display resolve despite escalation risk. Its declared deterrence purpose is retained as counterevidence, rather than assuming that it seeks war.

Educated assumption: The 2024 joint advisory attributes military-technology espionage to the DPRK intelligence apparatus; the 2025 NCSC review records continued military data theft. WithSecure’s January 2026 investigation independently identifies more recent Andariel activity. Infer acceptance of diplomatic exposure risk for intelligence advantage; attribution is an assessed finding, not a DPRK admission.

Educated assumption: Kim’s March 2026 rejection of nuclear disarmament for security guarantees weighs against negotiated capability reduction as the present policy. Qualified disagreement avoids claiming that preserving a nuclear arsenal necessarily rules out every limited conventional or numerical arms-control concession.

Educated assumption: The April 2026 rejection of external human-rights demands invokes national sovereignty and non-intervention, supporting final domestic control of law. Constitutional lawmaking powers sit with domestic institutions; accepted voluntary recommendations do not concede external supremacy.

Educated assumption: The September foreign-minister statement rejects denuclearisation demanded under Security Council resolutions when it conflicts with core sovereign interests. This directly supports opposition to unwanted binding external decisions; it is not a finding that the legal obligations cease to exist.

Educated assumption: Domestic sovereignty and rejection of external criminal accountability make domestic final authority the likely conflict preference. No general precedence provision covering every international court was verified.

Educated assumption: The Russia treaty is indefinite and limits each party’s freedom through mutual defence and constraints on adverse third-state arrangements. Its entry into force and troop deployment show an operative long-term alliance, not merely a diplomatic promise.

Educated assumption: The 2025 UPR response rejected recommendations concerning the Rome Statute and the commission-of-inquiry accountability process. Infer opposition to binding international criminal jurisdiction over its officials, qualified by the narrower reach of this evidence than every possible interstate tribunal.

Educated assumption: The September 2026 foreign minister prioritises retention of nuclear weapons as a core sovereign interest over denuclearisation demanded pursuant to Security Council resolutions. That is an explicit choice of national policy over an international institution’s conflicting goal.

Educated assumption: Sovereignty-focused cooperation favours nationally controlled environmental action rather than transferred decision authority. Moderate disagreement is a tentative delegation estimate, not denial of climate cooperation.

Educated assumption: Independent foreign policy remains prominent even within the Russia alliance. Moderate agreement against a compulsory common-policy bloc is likely; bilateral consultation is not equivalent to bloc-wide policy authority.

Educated assumption: The April 2026 foreign-ministry rejection of the Human Rights Council resolution treats country-specific external pressure as interference. Selective acceptance of UPR recommendations is voluntary cooperation, not recognition that those bodies can require domestic legal changes.

Educated assumption: The BTI report describes centralised monetary control; July 2026 reporting documents payment systems under the domestic central bank and a government-set forex accounting rate. Infer retention of national monetary authority. Use of dollars or yuan does not constitute a shared international monetary authority.

Educated assumption: Operative bilateral cooperation accepts shared commitments while retaining separate national decision structures. A conditional mixed response to pooled funding and governance is likely; a concrete general shared-governance mechanism was not verified.

Educated assumption: The immigration law places entry decisions with domestic agencies, and current consular guidance describes national permission procedures. Infer national control despite bilateral arrangements; reciprocal visa rules do not delegate admission decisions to an international institution.

Educated assumption: Articles 10–13 of the operative Russia treaty commit to negotiated economic and customs cooperation and mutual recognition of standards and certificates. This supports accepting some common negotiated trade rules while retaining wide national discretion; it does not claim WTO membership or verified implementation of every promised mechanism.

Educated assumption: The current territorial framework defines a separate sovereign state and removes reunification references, while the Russia partnership preserves distinct state institutions. Infer a preference to retain national policymaking rather than enter a political federation, without equating bilateral alliance duties with federal membership.

Educated assumption: Selective compliance and resistance to externally enforced nuclear and human-rights rules suggest prioritising immediate national interests when they conflict. Moderate disagreement is likely; no exact neutrality-versus-enforcement case was verified.

Educated assumption: Private commerce exists, but independent private ownership of most businesses is not the legal framework. State-linked enterprise and licensing control make strong disagreement the likelier response; informal markets qualify actual monopoly.

Educated assumption: The state retains ownership of essential economic networks and infrastructure. Strong agreement with public utility ownership is likely; household self-provision and informal investment do not establish legally private network ownership.

Educated assumption: The state prioritises public ownership even while allowing commercial managerial discretion. Moderate disagreement with a default private preference is likely; comparable-cost procurement comparisons were not verified.

Educated assumption: State enterprises operate beyond natural monopolies and are established in ordinary industrial and commercial sectors. Strong agreement is likely; informal capital participation does not mean those industries are left entirely to legal private owners.

Educated assumption: Medical facilities remain institutionally part of state provision, notwithstanding private fees and shortages. Moderate disagreement with generally private facility ownership is likely; privately buying medicine is not hospital ownership.

Educated assumption: Rail transport is reserved to state ownership. Strong agreement with publicly owned passenger rail infrastructure is likely; service quality and network scarcity do not alter the ownership framework.

Educated assumption: Public-service administration remains embedded in state provision with informal commercial involvement. Moderate disagreement with routine private-provider contracting is likely; exact comparable quality, access and cost tenders were not verified.

Educated assumption: State-owned banks are established and central to the financial system. Qualified agreement is likely with retaining them, although coexistence with ordinary licensed private banks is not implemented; informal private lenders are counterevidence to exclusive actual finance.

Educated assumption: Private investment generally uses state affiliations without independent legal business ownership. Strong disagreement with selling state commercial businesses to private owners is likely; management responsibility reforms are distinct from divestment.

Educated assumption: Housing allocation remains legally state based despite informal apartment sales. Public ownership of a substantial housing share is likely, while the rental category and stock share were not quantified.
Educated assumption: The national-security production system remains state controlled. Strong disagreement with ordinary private ownership is likely even when regulation could protect security.

Educated assumption: Resources are constitutionally reserved to the state and extraction is conducted through state-linked businesses. Informal investment does not displace the legal ownership preference.

Educated assumption: Municipal administration is embedded in the state hierarchy. Routine private-service contracting is less likely than direct administration; no national waste-contracting dataset was verified.
Educated assumption: The framework prioritises strategic state ownership despite opportunities for revenue. Strong retention is likely; management discretion is distinct from sale of ownership.

Educated assumption: Poor performance has led to management reforms and informal investment rather than legally independent private ownership. Moderate disagreement with automatic sale is likely; each subsidised firm was not investigated.
Educated assumption: Broadcasting remains state-run and excludes independent private outlets. Strong agreement with retaining a national broadcaster is the likely ownership response.

Educated assumption: Protective tariffs are expressly retained alongside actual controlled external commerce. Strong agreement is likely without attributing foreign-imposed sanctions to domestic tariff choice.

Educated assumption: Trade licences and state monopoly remain central. Broad removal of barriers at domestic-industry cost is strongly unlikely; resumed imports are counterevidence to autarky, not liberalisation.

Educated assumption: Self-reliant production and planned public purchasing favour domestic suppliers. Moderate agreement estimates the lower-price trade-off, since procurement comparison rules were not verified.
Educated assumption: Foreign commerce is conducted through licensed state structures. Strong disagreement with unrestricted cheapest-source buying is likely; smuggling is not a legal entitlement.
Educated assumption: Self-reliant essential production favours protection despite higher costs. Moderate agreement is likely, qualified by heavy reliance on imports for shortages.

Educated assumption: Selective reciprocal commerce and domestic protection make unilateral broad liberalisation unlikely. Moderate disagreement remains an estimate; no comprehensive tariff-reciprocity schedule was found.

Educated assumption: State-directed industrial development favours protection for emerging production. The specific temporary import measure and consumer-price trade-off were not verified, so agreement is qualified.

Educated assumption: Foreign ventures use approved special arrangements rather than ordinary equal entry terms. Strong disagreement is likely; promotion of joint ventures does not confer unrestricted national treatment.

Educated assumption: Domestic agricultural capacity is a policy priority, making protective limits likely. Food imports during shortages qualify the estimate; no blanket agricultural import ban is asserted.

Educated assumption: Planned support and national economic protection weigh strongly against leaving domestic adjustment entirely to foreign competition. Continued imports do not remove this protective preference.
Educated assumption: Sovereignty-focused reciprocal relations suggest responding to adverse tariffs. Moderate agreement is provisional; a concrete retaliatory tariff case was not found.

Educated assumption: Distinct state-regulated import channels make strict equal product taxation less likely. Moderate disagreement is uncertain because a full current customs and product-tax comparison was unavailable.

Educated assumption: Protecting national production makes restrictions on subsidised foreign competitors likely. Moderate agreement is a tentative instrument estimate; a countervailing-duty statute was not verified.

Educated assumption: Trade cooperation is accepted, but protection and independent production remain central. Moderate disagreement with dependency-raising tariff elimination is likely; the Russia treaty is not verified general tariff abolition.

Educated assumption: Foreign ventures are constrained by state control of strategic economic assets. Strong agreement against foreign controlling ownership is likely, without claiming every joint venture is prohibited.

Educated assumption: Access to foreign online services is tightly restricted. Strong disagreement is likely; information controls are the implemented mechanism rather than a conventional services tariff.

Educated assumption: Enterprise managers have bounded discretion, but production remains subject to national plans. Moderate disagreement is likelier than treating informal market supply as entirely government-selected.

Educated assumption: Compulsory national economic planning and implementation discipline remain established. Strong agreement is likely; the failure to attain targets does not imply their voluntary character.

Educated assumption: Market prices exist alongside official pricing and enforcement. Moderate disagreement with generally free pricing captures the dual system; this is not a claim that all actual prices are administratively fixed.
Educated assumption: National and regional industrial investment programmes are centrally directed. Strong agreement is likely despite market financing and local implementation.

Educated assumption: Managerial commercial discretion is subordinate to state ownership and planning. Moderate disagreement with exclusively demand-led expansion and closure is likely; informal private activity is counterevidence.
Educated assumption: Official exchange and essential distribution controls favour price intervention. Moderate agreement is likely; shortages, informal prices and weak enforcement limit the claim.

Educated assumption: Independent private entry is not legally recognised and licences are politically controlled. Strong disagreement is likely; tolerated informal business is not a general right of entry.
Educated assumption: State banking is subordinate to national priorities. Strong agreement is the likely direction preference, notwithstanding weak loan intermediation and informal finance.

Educated assumption: Capital and foreign exchange transfers are controlled. Strong disagreement is likely; illegal transfers and covert state operations do not establish unrestricted private mobility.
Educated assumption: State plans channel resources toward selected industrial sectors. Strong agreement is likely, while off-budget financing and opaque accounts prevent quantifying every subsidy.

Educated assumption: Unofficial foreign cash and private financial services coexist with state monetary control. Moderate disagreement with legally competing privately issued currencies is likely; foreign sovereign currencies are not private issue.

Educated assumption: National labour administration and state wage determination make a legally set wage floor more likely than entirely private bargaining. The exact ordinary minimum-wage provision was not independently verified.

Educated assumption: National workplace allocation and wage structures weigh strongly against ordinary employer-worker bargaining as the general wage system. Informal market earnings do not replace the formal labour framework.

Educated assumption: The central bank is not independent and national economic direction prevails. Strong agreement with plan-supporting monetary direction is likely; no precise current interest-rate schedule is asserted.

Educated assumption: Legal housing allocation is state based despite informal market deals. Moderate disagreement with generally market-determined rents is likely; a comprehensive rent-control rule was not found.

Educated assumption: The economic plan and central cabinet coordinate ordinary production and distribution. Strong agreement is likely despite widespread informal commerce and implementation failures.

Educated assumption: Actual provision and revenue extraction leave extensive income stratification. Moderate disagreement is likelier for substantial tax-and-benefit equalisation; socialist ownership and public service promises are not cash redistribution measures.

Educated assumption: Official tax abolition and weak transfers make increased income taxation solely to equalise income unlikely. Moderate agreement remains qualified by compulsory fees and labour extraction; those are not verified progressive income-tax rates.

Educated assumption: Evidence of inadequate actual support outweighs guarantees of assistance. Moderate disagreement with a tax-financed stronger cash floor is likely; absence of resources alone does not demonstrate an explicit philosophical rejection.

Educated assumption: Actual material assistance is restricted and inadequate rather than substantially equalising living standards. Moderate agreement is an institutional estimate, not praise of failure or a claim that basic needs are met.

Educated assumption: Abolished formal general taxation and nonprogressive extraction make a substantially progressive income-tax system unlikely. Moderate disagreement is likely; opaque fees prevent asserting zero fiscal burdens.

Educated assumption: Market households retain unequal earnings while broad income equalisation is weak. Moderate agreement is the likely practical redistribution estimate; state predation means retention is insecure, not an individual-rights promise.

Educated assumption: Inheritance of personal property is recognised and a redistributive inheritance tax was not identified. Moderate disagreement is likelier, qualified by opaque compulsory payments.

Educated assumption: Able-bodied adults face work obligations and support concentrates on incapacity or special status. Time-limited working-age cash support is a plausible restrictive estimate; a precise benefit-duration statute was not verified.

Educated assumption: No implemented wealth-tax transfer programme was identified in the described fiscal framework. Moderate disagreement is likelier; coercive confiscation or ownership controls are not automatically redistributive transfers.

Educated assumption: Actual assistance remains modest and the formal tax system is abolished. Qualified agreement is likely, although prioritising military expenditure rather than taxpayer burden may better explain the observed allocation.

Educated assumption: Effective assistance does not generally finance ordinary social participation beyond survival. Moderate disagreement is the likelier practical response; constitutional cultural provision is counterevidence, not proof of adequate cash support.

Educated assumption: Formal tax abolition coexists with compulsory extraction and rhetoric to expand provision. A mixed priority is likelier than assuming tax cutting or cash expansion clearly controls current budget decisions.

Educated assumption: Universal employment promises and in-kind provision do not establish effective low-paid worker cash supplements. Moderate disagreement is likelier; detailed payroll top-ups were not verified.

Educated assumption: No verified progressive marginal income-rate schedule operates in the formally tax-abolished framework. Moderate agreement is likely, qualified by opaque contributions and unequal coercive burdens.

Educated assumption: Land is state or cooperative property rather than large private estates subject to compensated transfer to new individual owners. Moderate disagreement is likelier; historic redistribution is not this present-tense compensated policy.

Educated assumption: Formal material assistance targets incapacity, old age and people without support, while broader actual transfers are weak. Moderate agreement is likely; status privileges and nominal universal employment complicate eligibility.

Educated assumption: Civil socialist law rather than a particular religious teaching provides the state legal framework. Strong agreement is likely; the leader cult is political ideology and is not silently recoded as organised religion.
Educated assumption: Religious doctrine is not an official source of national legislation. Strong disagreement is likely despite tightly supervised religious organisations.
Educated assumption: State policy does not require religious leadership approval. Strong agreement is likely; subordinated religious bodies do not constitute clerical vetoes.

Educated assumption: The constitutional foundation is socialist state ideology rather than a recognised religion. Strong disagreement is likely; formal religious freedom is distinct from establishment.

Educated assumption: State schools do not cultivate a recognised religion. Moderate agreement is the likelier nonproselytising teaching estimate, although neutral comparative religion teaching itself was not verified.

Educated assumption: Political ideological instruction is central, but a state religion is not recognised. Strong disagreement is likely; political indoctrination is not treated as religious faith instruction.

Educated assumption: Courts administer civil state law under political control rather than clerical rulings. Strong agreement is likely; judicial dependence is assessed on democracy and does not establish religious jurisdiction.

Educated assumption: Lawmaking institutions provide no religious-authority review role. Strong disagreement is likely; representation in subordinate organisations does not create a required legislative review.

Educated assumption: Official ceremonies primarily use political and national symbolism. Moderate agreement is likely; the practice of every event and religious diplomatic occasion was not independently established.

Educated assumption: Autonomous religious activity is suppressed while selected religious sites serve supervised public purposes. Moderate disagreement with faith-strengthening public spending is likelier; site upkeep may be cultural or diplomatic rather than proselytising.

Educated assumption: Government buildings primarily endorse political leadership rather than a particular religion. Moderate agreement is an estimated display practice; every heritage building was not surveyed.

Educated assumption: National public identity and festivals are organised around state and revolutionary history rather than predominant-faith official recognition. Strong disagreement is likely without denying private religious observance.

Educated assumption: Religious-affiliated political organisations are subordinate to civil selection, not an established clergy-only seat entitlement. Moderate agreement is likely; all seat allocation rules were not verified.

Educated assumption: Formal tax abolition applies generally, so a special religion-specific exemption beyond charities is unlikely. Moderate disagreement is a tentative estimate because religious financial treatment was not separately documented.

Educated assumption: Marriage administration is civil rather than requiring clerical approval. Moderate agreement is likely; removing religious requirements is a hypothetical extension where such requirements were not identified.
Educated assumption: The state judicial framework does not establish binding religious family courts. Strong disagreement is likely; informal ritual does not create separate legal jurisdiction.

Educated assumption: Implemented cultural controls restrict change departing from prescribed national customs. Moderate disagreement is likely; state-led social reforms and women’s economic activity counter any claim of complete historical continuity.

Educated assumption: National cultural heritage and prescribed socialist family norms are actively maintained. Moderate agreement is likely, qualified by selective transformation of inherited practices.

Educated assumption: The reviewed family framework privileges heterosexual marriage and does not recognise diverse partnership families equally. Moderate disagreement is likely; all nonmarital households are not thereby legally excluded.

Educated assumption: Documented gendered workplace and family expectations persist despite formal equality. Moderate agreement is a practice-based estimate; equality legislation is retained as counterevidence.

Educated assumption: The legal family framework does not recognise same-sex marriage and rejects sexual-orientation diversity. Strong disagreement is likely; nonrecognition is not proof of a separately verified penal ban on consensual same-sex relations.

Educated assumption: Family law and official family harmony messaging favour the heterosexual married household. Moderate agreement is likely without claiming every single-parent family lacks assistance.

Educated assumption: Reproductive health provision and the lack of a clear general abortion ban coexist with reported coercion and birth-control constraints. A conditional mixed response is likely; absence of a ban does not establish social acceptance of elective early abortion.

Educated assumption: The state prescribes compulsory schooling and ideological content. Strong disagreement with a final parental veto is likely, independent of whether the taught sexual norms are traditional.

Educated assumption: The nonrecognition of same-sex partnership makes equal adoptive-parent acceptance strongly unlikely. Exact adoption eligibility was not verified; the response is an explicit institutional extension.

Educated assumption: Enforced cultural appearance and dress norms favour prescribed public modesty. Moderate agreement is likely; prohibitions on foreign fashions are not an exact universal modest-dress rule.

Educated assumption: Protected prescribed national language and nonrecognition of gender diversity favour retained conventions. Moderate disagreement is likely; a specific pronoun-policy text was not identified.

Educated assumption: Schools transmit state-approved moral and national customs. Moderate agreement is likely, qualified because socialist moral instruction can itself depart from older religious or feudal traditions.

Educated assumption: Persisting gendered expectations weigh against equal general acceptance of cross-sex roles. Moderate disagreement is likely; women in senior posts and market work are important exceptions, not proof of equal acceptance throughout.

Educated assumption: Institutional continuity and controlled social change favour gradual prescribed reform rather than popularity-driven rapid change. Moderate agreement is likely; leadership can also impose abrupt reforms without public consent.

Educated assumption: The state does not recognise sexual-orientation and gender diversity within its population and comprehensive sexual education is deficient. Strong disagreement with the inclusive curriculum proposal is likely.

Educated assumption: National heritage is preserved as a connection to earlier generations within a socialist framework. Moderate agreement is likely, qualified by selective removal of customs inconsistent with state ideology.

Educated assumption: Implemented digital systems and rapid strategic technology adoption favour use before every long-term effect is settled. Moderate agreement is the likelier general estimate; military adoption does not automatically define medical approval.

Educated assumption: Actual digital deployment and technology-led production weigh against restricting all new technologies to long-term trials. Moderate disagreement is likely while high-risk clinical regulation remains separately uncertain.

Educated assumption: Implemented large construction and regional industrial development favour substantial public infrastructure. Moderate agreement is likely, qualified by constitutional environmental protection and no verified project-specific habitat trade-off.

Educated assumption: State medical administration and external clinical cooperation make evidence-based restriction more likely for novel medicine. Moderate agreement is tentative; weak health capacity is not itself a verified long-term safety rule.

Educated assumption: Civilian automation and deployed AI-linked revenue systems show productivity-led adoption. Moderate agreement estimates acceptance of worker replacement; the exact retraining trade-off was not verified.

Educated assumption: Actual construction and industrial priorities outweigh ineffective environmental safeguards. Moderate disagreement is likely, qualified by reforestation and restoration campaigns.

Educated assumption: Food insecurity and technological agricultural modernisation make controlled cultivated-meat development plausible. Moderate agreement is a low-confidence estimate; no implemented cultivated-meat approval was verified.

Educated assumption: State-directed medical administration makes unrestricted invasive enhancement unlikely. Moderate agreement is the likelier research-first estimate, but no healthy-person implant rule or long-term standard was found.

Educated assumption: Technology-led development and continued energy-intensive production favour technological climate responses. Moderate agreement is likely; the exact comparison with consumption reduction was not verified.

Educated assumption: Actual accelerated construction and weak environmental enforcement weigh against generally delaying projects for uncertainty. Moderate disagreement is likely; formal prior environmental measures are meaningful counterevidence.

Educated assumption: Invasive healthy-person enhancement is unlikely to be available solely on minimal safety grounds under controlled medical administration. Moderate disagreement is tentative; an explicit permission threshold was not documented.

Educated assumption: Diagnostic reliability and supervised health provision favour controlled evaluation of clinical AI. Moderate agreement is the likelier estimate; actual cross-group validation rules were not verified.
